subject: Dedicated GPU pool packaging & pricing — Aurora Analytics
messages:
From: Ava Spencer <ava@aurora-analytics.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial sizing/pricing inquiry: Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Diego —

Thanks for taking a call last week. Aurora is trying to finalize a committed pricing conversation for a Dedicated GPU pool to support our recommendation engine. Before procurement pulls together PO terms we need a clearer sizing + pricing proposal so we can model TCO and put together an internal business case.

Quick context:
- Peak QPS: ~240 infer/sec across 3 regions, expected steady-state 120 infer/sec
- Typical payload: chat completions and reranking; mean context length ~1,600 tokens, 99th perc up to 4,000 tokens
- Concurrency: bursts up to 350 simultaneous sessions during campaigns
- SLA need: 99.9% availability; p95 generation latency target ~120ms

Can you share:
1) Recommended pool size (GPU types + count) for committed throughput and headroom
2) Pricing tiers for monthly reserved commits (12/24/36 mo) and suggested discount anchors
3) Any throughput guarantees or overage model (how we bill burst usage)

We can share a sample workload file if helpful.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call.

— Ava
Ava Spencer
Head of ML Infrastructure, Aurora Analytics
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Spencer <ava@aurora-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial sizing/pricing inquiry: Dedicated GPU pool

Ava —

Appreciate the details, that helps a lot. We can definitely support Aurora at scale; I have a few follow-ups so our sizing is conservative but cost-efficient:

1) Are those QPS numbers measured as token-generation requests or API calls? (some customers report QPS as messages/sec; we need tokens/sec profile)
2) What's the distribution of sequence lengths? You noted mean=1,600 and 99th=4,000 — can you share percentiles (p50/p75/p90/p95) if you have them?
3) How tolerant is your app to quantization? E.g., would 4-bit/8-bit model variants be acceptable for ~5% quality delta?
4) Do you need isolation per-region (separate pools) or are you okay with a single multi-region pool and regional failover?

I'll attach an initial pricing PDF and a short sizing checklist (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf). Marissa (pricing) and Ben (commercial) are looped in to prepare committed tiers and discount guidance. If you can, please attach that sample workload CSV and we'll run a quick capacity estimate.

Best,
Diego
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Thanks, Diego — answers below and attached a small sample of our traffic.

- QPS is API calls/sec; average tokens per API call ~85 (generation only), but for reranking calls we often send full-context scoring requests (tokens per call ~1,800).
- Percentiles for combined traffic: p50=70 tokens, p75=220 tokens, p90=900 tokens, p95=1,600 tokens, p99=3,200 tokens.
- Quality sensitivity: for customer-facing ranking we need high fidelity; 8-bit is acceptable for internal batch reranks but production ranking must be FP16 or mixed precision.
- Regional model placement: we need independent pools for US and EU for data residency; APAC can be served from US or partner cloud.

Attached: Aurora-sample-workload.csv (sample of 48 hours). Let me know if you want a larger dump.

— Ava
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 08:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial sizing/pricing inquiry: Dedicated GPU pool — Aurora context and SLAs

Team —

Forwarding Aurora's traffic sample and percentile breakdown. Key asks: EU + US separate pools, p95 latency target ~120ms, mixed workload with heavy long-context reranking. They expect 120 steady-state calls/sec across regions and 350 concurrent sessions at peak.

Quick ask: can pricing + commit tiers be modeled with two pool options:
A) Conservative: Guarantee p95 latency and throughput with 20% headroom — higher commit, smaller per-token price; include SLA credit of 5% of monthly bill for downtime beyond 99.9%.
B) Flexible: Lower committed throughput with burst overage policy (pre-negotiated burst cap per month) — lower up-front commit, higher per-token for bursts.

Please propose GPU types (recommendations between A100-80GB, H100, or M60-like inference instances), suggested counts per region, pricing anchors for 12/24/36 mo, and an initial discount range we can show Aurora (we should be competitive but protect NRR). Also note any SOW or procurement docs (SOW-draft-Aurora.docx).

Diego
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial sizing/pricing inquiry: Dedicated GPU pool — Aurora context and SLAs

Diego / Ben —

Notes from sizing run (ran Aurora-sample-workload.csv through our estimator):
- Recommended baseline per-region: 6x H100 (80GB equiv) for US, 4x H100 for EU. Rationale: long-context reranking drives KV cache and memory needs; H100 preferred for latency headroom.
- With those pools, steady-state sustained throughput = ~150 infer/sec (US) and 100 infer/sec (EU) with p95 latencies ~85-110ms for typical payloads; burst headroom up to 300-350 concurrent sessions if autoscaling/burst enabled but will require short-lived spot expansion or pre-purchased burst buffer.
- Conservative option (A): commit to 130/90 steady-state (US/EU) across 24-month contract. Pricing anchor: list $X per GPU-hour, suggested effective discount for 24mo commit = 28-33% off list for the committed units + 15% discount on additional capacity if exercised within burst cap. Include SLA credit = 5% of monthly bill for >0.1% downtime beyond 99.9%.
- Flexible option (B): commit to 90/60 steady-state across 12-month with burst pool allowed up to 40% of committed capacity billed at 1.6x rate; suggested discount = 18-22% on committed units.

Action items:
- Ben: confirm commercial can offer 28% top-line discount for 24mo with marketing-approved reference clause and a standard crediting SLA.
- Diego: I'll draft the pricing grid and SOW changes; will attach redlined SOW.

Marissa
VP, Product Pricing — Redwood Inference

Ava / Diego / Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough thread. Commercial is ok to present two options: the 24mo conservative commit at 30% discount (midpoint of Marissa's range) with a 5% SLA credit and a 12mo flexible commit at 20% discount with burst billing at 1.6x. We'll include a 90-day exit clause tied to usage floors if Aurora's usage materially undershoots projections.

Next steps for Aurora:
1) Diego will send a formal proposal PDF with the pricing grid and pool configuration.
2) If Aurora agrees in principle, procurement will be given a redlined SOW and a DocuSign envelope for the Master Services Agreement.
3) We can schedule a technical onboarding runbook call to finalize autoscaling/burst controls.

Ava — can you confirm whether procurement prefers a single PO for both regions or separate POs per region? That will change invoicing and contract language.

Ben Carter
Head of Commercial — Redwood Inference
